title: Nouns and articles: le, la, les, un, une, des
summary: Every French noun is masculine or feminine: learn le, la, l', les, un, une, des, the silent plural, and how to name things with c'est and voici.
focus: Gender, definite and indefinite articles, and the plural of nouns
content:
## Every noun is masculine or feminine

Every French noun has a gender, even things: **le livre** (the book) is masculine, **la table** (the table) is feminine. There is no neuter, and the gender is rarely logical, so learn each noun with its article.

| the | masculine | feminine |
|---|---|---|
| one | **le** livre | **la** table |
| one, before a vowel or silent h | **l'**ami | **l'**amie, **l'**heure |
| several | **les** livres | **les** tables |

**Le** and **la** drop their vowel before a vowel sound: **l'ordinateur**, **l'école**, **l'hôtel**. **Les** is the same for both genders. Before a vowel its s is heard as a z: **les amis** (lay-za-mee).

## A, an, some: un, une, des

- **un** with a masculine noun: **un canapé** (a sofa)
- **une** with a feminine noun: **une chaise** (a chair)
- **des** with any plural: **des livres** (books, some books)

English often leaves *some* out, but French never leaves out **des**. **Voici des chaises.** (Here are some chairs.) **Un** and **une** never drop a letter: **un ami**, **une amie**, with the n linked to the vowel in speech.

## One, two, many: the plural

Add **-s**: **la chaise → les chaises**. The -s is silent, so you hear the plural in the article: **le livre** / **les livres**.

- Nouns in **-eau** and most in **-eu** take **-x**: **le bateau → les bateaux**, **le jeu → les jeux**.
- Most nouns in **-al** become **-aux**: **le journal → les journaux**.
- Nouns already ending in **-s**, **-x** or **-z** stay the same: **le bras → les bras**, **le prix → les prix**.

## Gender clues, c'est and voici

Some endings give the gender away, with a few exceptions:

| feminine | masculine |
|---|---|
| **-tion, -sion**: la station, la télévision | **-age**: le fromage, le garage (but la plage, la page) |
| **-euse** for a woman: la vendeuse | **-eur** for a man: le vendeur |

To name a thing: **C'est un livre.** (It's a book.) **C'est une fenêtre.** **Ce sont des chaises.** (They're chairs.) To point, use **voici** (here is, here are) and **voilà** (there is, there you go). **Voici le salon, et voilà le chat !**

vocabulary.example: C'est une grande table.
Voici quatre chaises.
C'est le livre de Marie.
Le chat dort sur le canapé.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

vocabulary.example: Voilà la fenêtre du salon.
La télévision est dans le salon.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The television is in the living room.

vocabulary.example: C'est un chat noir.
Voici l'amie de Paul, Sophie.
Voilà des bateaux sur la Seine.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There are some boats on the Seine.

vocabulary.meaning: here is, here are / there is, there are
vocabulary.example: Voici le salon, et voilà la cuisine !
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's the living room, and there's the kitchen!

quiz.explanation: Fenêtre is feminine and starts with a consonant: la fenêtre.
hints: Feminine, no vowel at the start.

quiz.explanation: Ami starts with a vowel, so le becomes l': l'ami.
hints: What happens to le before a vowel?

quiz.prompt: The plural of le bateau is…
quiz.explanation: Nouns in -eau take -x in the plural, and the article becomes les: les bateaux.

quiz.prompt: Look at the endings. Which noun is feminine?
quiz.explanation: Nouns in -sion and -tion are feminine: la télévision. Nouns in -age are usually masculine: le fromage, le garage.
Chaise is feminine, so a chair is une chaise.
Any plural noun takes des for some: des livres. French never leaves it out.
hints: The plural of un and une.

quiz.explanation: Most nouns just add a silent -s: les chats.

quiz.prompt: In les tables, the final -s of tables is pronounced.
quiz.explanation: False. The plural -s is silent: table and tables sound the same. You hear the plural in les.
hints: Where do you hear the plural?

quiz.prompt: Voilà le canapé ! means There's the sofa!
quiz.explanation: True. Voilà points at something: there is, there you go.

guide.tip: Never learn a noun alone: not livre but le livre, not chaise but une chaise. The article carries the gender.

concept.title: Same word, two genders
concept.markdown: A few nouns change meaning with their gender: **le livre** (book) / **la livre** (pound), **le tour** (turn, tour) / **la tour** (tower), **le poste** (job, set) / **la poste** (post office). This is another reason to learn the article with the noun.

bites.title: Le or la
bites.rule: Every noun is masculine (le) or feminine (la), even things. Before a vowel both become l'. Plural: les.
bites.example: le livre, la table, l'ami, les chaises
bites.example_meaning: the book, the table, the friend, the chairs

bites.title: Un, une, des
bites.rule: Un with a masculine noun, une with a feminine one, des with any plural. French never drops des.
bites.example: Voici un canapé et des chaises.
bites.example_meaning: Here are a sofa and some chairs.

bites.title: The silent plural
bites.rule: Add -s, which you don't hear: les chaises. -eau takes -x (les bateaux), -al becomes -aux. You hear the plural in les and des.

bites.title: Gender clues
bites.rule: -tion and -sion are feminine (la télévision), and -age is usually masculine (le fromage). Name a thing with c'est un / c'est une.

sorts.title: Le or la?
sorts.why: Learn the gender with each noun. -tion and -sion are feminine, and -age is usually masculine.

sorts.title: How does the plural end?
sorts.why: Most nouns add -s, -eau and -eu add -x, and nouns already ending in -s, -x or -z stay the same.

spots.why: Nouns in -eau take -x in the plural.
Before a vowel, la becomes l': l'amie.
After deux the noun is plural: deux livres.

builds.text: Ce sont des chaises et une table.

realm.content:
## Le butin à Eldmark

Open the chest after the dungeon and sort your loot. In the pile, **une épée** and **une potion** are feminine, **un bouclier** and **un parchemin** masculine. Several? **des potions**, **les boucliers**. Before a vowel: **l'épée**, **l'elfe**. Show it off with **C'est une épée !** **Voilà le butin !**

vocabulary.example: Voilà la table de la taverne.
C'est le livre de la mage.
C'est le chat de Séla la mage.
Voici l'ami de Borin, un nain.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here is Borin's friend, a dwarf.

vocabulary.example: Voilà le butin !
Voici la fenêtre de la tour.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here is the window of the tower.

vocabulary.example: C'est une épée magique.
Voici deux boucliers.
Le butin est dans le donjon.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The loot is in the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: Voilà des potions pour la quête.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There are some potions for the quest.

bites.title: Trier le butin
bites.rule: Loot has a gender too: une épée, une potion (f); un bouclier, un parchemin (m). Several: des épées, les boucliers.
bites.example: Voilà une épée et des potions.
bites.example_meaning: There's a sword and some potions.

listening.meaning: Here's a sword.

listening.text: C'est le bouclier de Borin.
listening.meaning: It's Borin's shield.

listening.text: Voilà des potions et un parchemin.
listening.meaning: There are some potions and a scroll.

listening.text: Les épées sont dans le coffre.
listening.meaning: The swords are in the chest.
listening.note: New word: le coffre = the chest.

listening.text: L'elfe et le nain regardent le butin.
listening.meaning: The elf and the dwarf are looking at the loot.

builds.meaning: Here are a sword and a shield.

spots.sentence: Le elfe est dans la taverne.
spots.why: Before a vowel, le becomes l': l'elfe.

sorts.title: Masculine or feminine loot?
sorts.why: Une épée, une potion, une quête; un bouclier, un parchemin, un butin.

quiz.explanation: The plural adds a silent -s: deux boucliers.

meadowbrook.content:
## Le panier à Meadowbrook

Your basket fills up at the market. In it, **une fraise** and **une citrouille** are feminine; **un champignon** and **un œuf** masculine. Several: **des fraises**, **les champignons**. Rosa points at the shelf: **Voici les graines !** And on the farm: **la vache**, **le mouton**, **les poules**.

vocabulary.example: Voilà le chat de la ferme.
Les fraises sont sur la table.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The strawberries are on the table.

vocabulary.example: Une poule à la fenêtre !
C'est l'amie de Rosa, Nora.
Voilà les graines, Nora !
Voici le bateau de Léo le pêcheur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here is Léo the fisherman's boat.

vocabulary.example: C'est une fraise de la ferme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's a strawberry from the farm.

vocabulary.example: Voici des champignons de la forêt.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here are some mushrooms from the forest.

vocabulary.example: Les poules sont dans le jardin.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hens are in the garden.

bites.title: Le panier
bites.rule: Crops and animals have a gender: une fraise, une poule (f); un champignon, un mouton (m). Plural: des fraises, les moutons.
bites.example: Voici des fraises et un champignon.
bites.example_meaning: Here are some strawberries and a mushroom.

listening.meaning: Here's a strawberry.

listening.meaning: It's Léo's boat.

listening.meaning: There are some mushrooms from the forest.

listening.meaning: Here are some pumpkin seeds, Nora.

sorts.why: Une fraise, une poule, une citrouille; un champignon, un mouton, un cochon.

rustwake.content:
## Le sac du fouilleur à Rustwake

Back from the ruined mall, empty your bag. Inside, **une boîte de conserve** and **une radio** are feminine; **un écrou**, **un disque** and **un tonique** masculine. Before a vowel: **l'écrou**, **l'armure**. Several: **des écrous**, **les disques**. Marta looks: **C'est un disque ! Voilà des écrous.**

vocabulary.example: Voici un livre de la station-service.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's a book from the gas station.

vocabulary.example: Les écrous sont sur la table de Marta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The nuts are on Marta's table.

vocabulary.example: Voilà un chat dans les ruines.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There's a cat in the ruins.

vocabulary.example: C'est l'ami de Léo le fouilleur.
Voici l'eau filtrée, et voilà le soda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's the filtered water, and there's the soda.

vocabulary.example: C'est une télévision de l'ancien monde.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's a television from the old world.

vocabulary.example: Voilà dix écrous.
C'est un disque de jazz.
Voici des boîtes de conserve.

bites.title: Le sac du fouilleur
bites.rule: Scrap has a gender: une radio, une boîte (f); un écrou, un disque (m). Before a vowel: l'écrou. Plural: des écrous, les disques.
bites.example: Voici un disque et des écrous.
bites.example_meaning: Here are a record and some nuts.

spots.why: Before a vowel, le becomes l': l'écrou.

sorts.title: Masculine or feminine scrap?
sorts.why: Un écrou, un disque, un tonique; une radio, une boîte, une armure.

quiz.explanation: Écrou starts with a vowel, so the article is l'. With un it stays un écrou.
